paper_sections.title: Salience Network Activity in Perceptual Decisions.
Experiment 3: audio-visual asynchrony and synchrony perception task

description.value: The study examined salience-network activity and directed functional interactions between the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and bilateral anterior insulae during four perceptual decision-making tasks with experimentally varied difficulty.

design.value: Participants completed four perceptual decision-making tasks involving face-house discrimination, happy-angry face discrimination, audiovisual asynchrony and synchrony perception, and random dot motion direction discrimination. Task difficulty was varied through stimulus noise, audiovisual temporal asynchrony, or motion coherence, and BOLD activity and directed functional connections among salience-network nodes were examined.

name.value: human participants who completed all four experimental tasks

description.value: There were 32 human participants (16 males, 16 females; mean age±standard deviation=27.6±4.7 years) who completed all four experimental tasks.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal or corrected to normal vision

exclusion_criteria.value: No participant reported difficulties recognizing red and green dots during practice session hence no red/green color blindness was reported.

description.value: One more male participant took part in face-house discrimination and in audiovisual asynchrony and synchrony perception tasks.

task_description.value: Participants discriminated images of faces and houses. Images were equalized for luminance and degraded by image pixel phase randomization with addition of Gaussian noise to produce 0%, 40%, and 55% noise levels.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to indicate their decisions as quickly and as accurately as possible; houses were indicated by right responses and faces by left responses.

stimuli.value: 14 images of faces and 14 images of houses, equalized for luminance and degraded with image pixel phase randomization and Gaussian noise; visual stimuli subtended 4.34° by 6.08° visual angles.

task_description.value: Participants discriminated happy and angry human face images presented as clear or noisy images.

instructions.value: Participants indicated happy faces with left responses and angry faces with right responses.

stimuli.value: Two sets of human face images, a happy set and an angry set, each consisting of eight images, four males and four females; images were presented with 0% or 40% noise.

task_name.value: audio-visual asynchrony and synchrony perception task

task_description.value: Participants judged whether paired auditory and visual stimuli were synchronous or asynchronous. The audiovisual task also included multisensory and unisensory blocks.

instructions.value: Participants reported their perception by left responses if they perceived synchrony or right responses for asynchrony.

stimuli.value: A 440-Hz-30-ms tone paired with a 30-ms yellow-red disc flash of 0.7 cm radius; the flash was presented centrally and the beep was delivered through a pair of earphones.

task_name.value: random dot motion (RDM) direction discrimination task

task_description.value: Participants discriminated the leftward or rightward direction of randomly moving noisy dot fields. Difficulty was manipulated using color coherence and color incoherence conditions and different coherence levels.

instructions.value: Participants reported leftward-moving dots with left responses and rightward-moving dots with right responses.

stimuli.value: Randomly moving noisy fields of dots presented within a circular aperture. The aperture had a diameter of 7.5 cm; dots were red and green and moved at 3° to 7°/s with a density of 16.7 dots per deg2/s.

instrument.value: 3-Tesla Siemens scanner available at the Georgia State University and Georgia Institute of Technology Center for Advanced Brain Imaging, Atlanta, Georgia

description.value: Functional scans were acquired with a T2*-weighted gradient echo-planar imaging protocol. Each functional session started with 30 sec of initial rest and ended with 35 sec of final rest. Participants performed the face-house task in three functional runs.

description.value: High-resolution anatomical images were acquired for anatomical references.

MRI data were analyzed using Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM8), including slice timing correction, motion correction, coregistration to the individual anatomical image, normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute template, and spatial smoothing of the normalized image with an 8-mm isotropic Gaussian kernel.

spatial smoothing with an 8-mm isotropic Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: A separate GLM was specified according to the task sequences and behavioral responses for each participant. Only correct trials for each condition, rest, and six motion parameters were included; the six motion parameters were entered as nuisance covariates and regressed out of the data.

Individual contrast images from the first-level analysis were entered into a second-level analysis for a separate one-sample t-test. A random-effect, model-based, univariate statistical analysis was performed in a two-level procedure.

Time courses were extracted from three 6-mm-radius spherical ROIs in dACC, left insula, and right insula. BOLD time series were hemodynamically deconvolved. The optimal autoregressive model order was selected by comparing parametric and nonparametric power spectra. Time-domain Granger causality values were obtained by integrating causality spectra over the entire frequency range. Significance thresholds were based on at least 1000 random permutations and a gamma-distribution fit at p<10−3.

estimator.value: parametric spectral Granger causality with permutation-based thresholding and conditional Granger causality
